anomalies.observed: In the 'ATO Valve' block the low-side switch MOSFET T6 is a 30 V AO3400A (SOT-23), driven through R27 100R/NET0004 with a BT3904 (T7) pre-driver and a 10k pull-up (R40). The 60 V AON6407 that the spec reserves for the valve instead sits in the 'reverse polarity protection' position of the POWER TRAIN (T8).
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table assigns the 60 V AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) to the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch (T3 in the spec's numbering), precisely because it must block the 24 V rail plus solenoid flyback/switching transients. A 30 V part in that position is under-rated.

anomalies.impact: The ATO valve switch is populated with a 30 V MOSFET on a 24 V inductive load whose turn-off spikes and rail transients (TVS clamps at 28 V) can exceed 30 V, exposing T6 to avalanche stress and premature failure; its higher RdsOn also increases dissipation. The two MOSFETs (AON6407 and AO3400A) appear to have been swapped between the valve and the reverse-polarity positions relative to the intended design.
